statement.text: For a digraph <math> D=(V,A) </math>, we call a nonempty <math> C\subseteq A </math> a '''dicut''' if there is some <math> X\subseteq V </math> such that no edge enters <math> X </math> and <math> C </math> consists of the outgoing edges of <math> X </math>. The conjecture states that for any <math> D </math>, there exists a system <math> \mathcal{C} </math> of pairwise disjoint finite dicuts and an edge set <math> F\subseteq A </math>  consisting of one edge from each element of <math> \mathcal{C} </math>, such that <math>F</math> intersects every finite dicut of <math> D </math>.
